prompts.text: Name a type of shot in a sport (like a free throw or a drop shot)

items.quip: Antonín Panenka chipped the winning penalty in the 1976 Euro final.
items.title: Panenka (penalty kick)
items.description: Type of penalty kick notably used in the 1976 European Championship
items.extract: In association football, the panenka is a technique used while taking a penalty kick in which the taker, instead of kicking the ball to the left or right of the goalkeeper, gives a light touch underneath the ball, causing it to rise and fall within the centre of the goal, deceiving the goalkeeper who will most likely have committed to a dive away from the centre.

items.quip: Rabona takes its name from Argentine slang for skipping school.
items.title: Rabona
items.extract: In association football, the rabona is the technique of kicking the football where the kicking leg is crossed behind the back of the standing leg.

prompts.text: Name a part of a shoe

items.quip: Aglet comes from the Old French aguillette, meaning little needle.
items.title: Aglet
items.description: Sheath on the end of a shoelace or cord
items.extract: An aglet or aiglet is a small sheath, often made of plastic or metal, attached at each end of a shoelace, a cord, or a drawstring. An aglet keeps the fibers of the lace or cord from unraveling; its firmness and narrow profile make it easier to hold and easier to feed through eyelets, lugs, or other lacing guides.

items.quip: A Goodyear welt lets cobblers resole the same shoe repeatedly.

prompts.text: Name a country whose name ends in N

items.quip: Rainforest covers nearly ninety percent of Gabon.
items.title: Gabon
items.extract: Gabon, officially the Gabonese Republic, is a country on the Atlantic coast of Central Africa, lying on the equator. It is bordered by Equatorial Guinea to the northwest, Cameroon to the north, the Republic of the Congo to the east and south, while sharing a maritime border with São Tomé and Príncipe to the west in the Gulf of Guinea. It has an area of 270,000 square kilometres (100,000 sq mi) and a population of 2.6 million people. There are coastal plains, mountains, and savanna in the east. Libreville is the capital and largest city; other major cities include Port-Gentil and Franceville.

items.quip: Japan's first glaciers were only officially recognised in 2012.
items.title: Japan
items.extract: Japan is an island country in East Asia. Located in the Pacific Ocean off the northeast coast of the Asian mainland, it is bordered to the west by the Sea of Japan, the Sea of Okhotsk in the north, and the East China Sea in the south. The Japanese archipelago consists of four major islands alongside over 14,000 smaller islands. Japan is divided into 47 administrative prefectures and eight traditional regions, and around 75% of its terrain is mountainous and heavily forested, concentrating its agriculture and highly urbanized population along its eastern coastal plains. With a population of almost 123 million as of 2026, it is the world's 11th most populous country. Tokyo is the country's capital and largest city.

prompts.text: Name a standard type of tax

items.quip: Japan levies a hot spring tax on each onsen bath.
Zakat asks Muslims to give 2.5 percent of their wealth yearly.
items.title: Zakat
items.description: Form of almsgiving obligatory in Islam
items.extract: Zakat is one of the Five Pillars of Islam. Zakat is the Arabic word for "giving to charity" or "giving to the needy". Zakat is a form of almsgiving, often collected by the Muslim Ummah. It is considered in Islam a religious obligation, and by Quranic ranking, is next after prayer (salah) in importance. Eight heads of zakat are mentioned in the Quran.

prompts.text: Name a type of bird (bare bird names like owl or finch, no species or subspecies)

items.quip: Hoatzin chicks hatch with claws on their wings for climbing.
items.title: Hoatzin
items.description: Species of bird in South America
items.extract: The hoatzin is a species of tropical bird found in swamps, riparian forests, and mangroves of the Amazon and Orinoco Basins in South America. It is the only extant species in the genus Opisthocomus which is the only extant genus in the family Opisthocomidae under the order Opisthocomiformes. Despite being the subject of intense debate by specialists, the taxonomic position of this family is still far from clear.

items.quip: Oilbirds navigate dark caves by echolocation and eat only fruit.
items.title: Oilbird
items.extract: The oilbird, locally known as the guácharo, is a bird species found in the northern areas of South America including the Caribbean island of Trinidad. It is the only living species in the genus Steatornis, the family Steatornithidae, and the order Steatornithiformes. Nesting in colonies in caves, oilbirds are nocturnal feeders on the fruits of the oil palm and tropical laurels. They are the only nocturnal flying fruit-eating birds in the world. They forage at night, with specially adapted eyesight. However, they navigate by echolocation in the same way as bats, one of the few birds to do so. They produce a high-pitched clicking sound of around 2 kHz that is audible to humans.
